author: Andyfx
text:
The Engulf - FTR combo is one of my favorite trade setup for a quick scalp.

If we are moving away from an HTF SD zone, I wait for an Engulf of previous high/low, then I take the trade if the FTR touch the SD pocket at the origin of the engulf. In fact it is trading SD pockets of a CP zone, subsequents Engulf and FTR to SD pocket at the origin of the Engulf. Like it is the FTB to previous FTR again and again after an engulf.

Just make sure of not buying near supply and selling near demand, and that the SD pocket is tight and clean with a strong move away making the engulf. Look to the left and take the trade only if there is free space or even better an engulf of previous opposite FTR SD pocket into a new PAZ, or wait for an Engulf of a FL and enter on the second FTR wich is FTBing the FTR SD pocket. The QM is also a powerfull Engulf-FTR setup.

Edit: an other option to trade ENG+ FTR combo: in strong momentum trends, price will often bounce at SR flip instead of origin-of-the-engulf-SD-pocket, if we are not sure we can split the position in 2: open one at SR flip and one if the price touch SD pocket, same stop loss above SD pocket for both.

Something like this FTR to FTR SD pocket

FTR to SRFlip

market. You are doing a great work and I'm sure that soon you'll become an awesome trader and maybe I can learn from you.

Talking about ENG+FTR, to me a FTR is the pullback that forms AFTER an Engulf of something relevant in that timeframe (previous High/Low, FL, previous SD zone, SR level etc). I think that FTR are there because some positions are closed and to bring price back at a better price and fill more orders (and trap breakout traders), and very often they form new SD pockets that can be traded if the move is strong and if there is a new engulf confirming the direction and stuff.

Edit: this can be also a FL with some bounces if there was an engulf of something left. (the FTR I'm referring to is that in the low of the chart you marked)

If later I have more time I try to look at others.

Anyways keep in mind that I'm absolutely not sure of what I think.

Have a nice day

Here is another interesting chart I really enjoyed creating, I will try to explain it the best I can, the year is 2008, and it's the AUD.

First up is the 4hr chart, I have marked the top supply the ultimate supply purely for the reason we were in a massive uptrend. we see the lows get engulfed, and price attempted to get back into the ultimate supply, but 'Failed', here we have an FTR, I am definitely enjoying drilling down to the LTFs for, 1 to reduce risk, and 2, to pin point my trade more accurately.

So, we move down to the hourly, everything is left in place as per the 4hr. The first thing I noticed was the obvious FL (Green), I know this could be called an FTR, but from my experience whilst studying FL, this struck me as a FL here, I also noticed the FTR (Green) and the 2 engulfs below and the CP, but this was not good enough, so I moved down to the 15 min..

All zones have been left on the chart. The first thing I noticed straight away was how prominent the green FTR looked, and also looking to the left of that we can also see another FTR that created the green FTR., but if we look in the FL from the hourly, look how beautiful the yellow FTR looks, lovely looking base, price CPing up, I think this would be a good trade.

Any comments are welcome.

DT

Hi Dr,

If I was trading this chart live, I do not believe this area I have marked 'FTR' would even be an FTR as price would have needed to engulf the high which I have marked on the chart below.

So, once price did in fact engulf the high and keep on rallying I believed this was an FTR, price failed to hit demand which I believe was support. The small FTB was only fully realised and respected once price did engulf the high making the zone an FTR and the pin to the level and FTB.
